result.title: A new algorithmic approach for finding flat minima: critically damped Polyak stepsizes
result.summary: We present a new adaptive stepsize rule that biases gradient descent toward flatter minima in both theory and practice, and establish the first uniform-in-time guarantees for both sharpness and loss reduction for a broad class of locally quadratic objectives. Our critically damped Polyak (CDP) stepsizes multiply the classical Polyak rule by $4$ and a mild damping factor. The factor $4$ is critical in that it produces equioscillations around the manifold of minimizers $\mathcal{M}$ to leading order. Damping provably drives convergence to $\mathcal{M}$. CDP thus operates at the edge of stability by adapting its stepsizes to local curvature. Once the loss is small, its projected iterates follow gradient descent on $\log{λ_1(\nabla^2 \mathcal{L})}$ along $\mathcal{M}$ to leading order, paralleling the flatness bias of normalized gradient descent (Arora et al., 2022). Unlike normalized gradient descent, CDP step lengths shrink with the distance to $\mathcal{M}$, enabling convergence to an interpolating solution that locally minimizes sharpness at finite learning rate. We establish our theory for a broad class of non-negative losses with locally quadratic Morse-Bott structure near $\mathcal{M}$, capturing regular interpolation regimes in smooth overparameterized neural networks. Empirically, CDP stepsizes produce a flattening effect similar to that of Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM, Foret et al., 2021), reducing sharpness even in settings beyond our theory, including nonlinear teacher-student networks and fine-tuning of pre-trained LLMs.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出「临界阻尼 Polyak」（CDP）自适应步长规则：将经典 Polyak 步长乘以 4 并加入阻尼因子，使梯度下降在局部二次型目标上沿极小值流形等幅振荡并收敛，从而在有限学习率下偏向更平坦的极小点，并在非线性 teacher-student 网络与 LLM 微调中观察到类似 SAM 的锐度下降效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 这是纯优化理论工作，与视觉证据或 latent 状态生成无直接联系，但其向平坦极小的步长调度可能可供核查：在训练 looped/latent 推理模型时能否通过控制锐度改善长序列与深层循环的稳定性及泛化。
